summary: Converts a double value to a sign/width-formatted string. Reads the double through a1, formats it via LocaleAwareStringFormat into a local 24-byte buffer and a 4-dword scratch array, then applies sign-aware width handling by calling sub_5955AA with an adjusted width (adding 1 when the formatted text starts with '-' and when a3 is positive) and finally sub_58BE2E with the original a2, a3, a4 and the scratch array. Returns a2.

local_names.a1: pointer to the double value to format
local_names.a2: width argument propagated to both helpers and returned
local_names.a3: precision/width-related argument used to compute the adjusted width
local_names.a4: output pointer passed through to sub_58BE2E

operations.description: Read the double value v5 through a1 (low/high 32-bit halves passed to the formatter)
LocaleAwareStringFormat(SLOBYTE(v5), HIDWORD(v5), v7, v6): format the double into scratch array v7 and 24-byte buffer v6

Compute adjusted width as (v7[0] == 45) + a2 + (a3 > 0), i.e. add 1 for a leading '-' sign character in the formatted text and add 1 when a3 is positive, then call sub_5955AA(adjusted_width, a3 + 1, v7)
sub_58BE2E(a2, a3, a4, v7, 0): apply the width/sign formatting using the scratch array and original width arguments

unresolved: The exact behavior of sub_58BE2E and sub_5955AA (padding, truncation, or width application) is not established from this function alone.
The role of the 24-byte local buffer v6 versus the 4-dword scratch v7 is unclear; v6 may be an intermediate formatted string that is only consumed later.
The check v7[0] == 45 is interpreted as detecting a leading '-' sign to reserve width for negative numbers, but the formatter's exact output layout is unverified.
The semantics of the returned a2 value (width versus count) and its contract with the caller CfltcvtCRTFloatConversionDispatch are unknown.
